name: Universal Studios Hollywood
address: 100 Universal City Plaza, Universal City, CA 91608
description: Theme park with Wizarding World, the studio tour, and new Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift coaster opening 2026.
must_try: Studio Tour backlot tram and the new coaster.

name: Olvera Street
address: 845 N Alameda St, Los Angeles, CA 90012
description: The birthplace of Los Angeles. A vibrant Mexican marketplace since 1930 — taquitos, shops, Dia de los Muertos celebrations.
must_try: Cielito Lindo taquitos and the Avila Adobe (oldest house in LA).

name: Griffith Observatory
address: 2800 E Observatory Rd, Los Angeles, CA 90027
description: Free admission, insane views of the Hollywood Sign and downtown skyline. Come at sunset — non-negotiable.
must_try: Sunset from the west terrace.

name: Hollywood Forever Cemetery
description: Final resting place of Rudolph Valentino, Judy Garland, and more. Summer Cinespia movie screenings are essential.
must_try: Cinespia outdoor movie screening (summer).

name: La Brea Tar Pits
description: Active paleontological dig site in the middle of the city. Watch scientists excavate Ice Age fossils.
must_try: Watch the ongoing excavation from the observation pit.

name: Venice Canals
description: Quiet, charming canals lined with eclectic homes. A world away from the boardwalk chaos just blocks over.
must_try: Walk the bridges at golden hour.

name: Walt Disney Concert Hall
address: 111 S Grand Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90012
description: Frank Gehry's stainless steel masterpiece. Even if you skip the concert, walk the exterior and garden.
must_try: Self-guided architecture tour (free).

name: Watts Towers
description: Simon Rodia spent 33 years building these 17 interconnected structures from found objects. A folk art masterpiece.
must_try: Guided tour of the towers.

name: Academy Museum of Motion Pictures
description: The Oscars museum. Film history from silent era to Marvel, plus a stunning Renzo Piano sphere theater.
must_try: The Spielberg Gallery and the dome theater.

name: California Science Center
address: 700 Exposition Park Dr, Los Angeles, CA 90037
description: Free admission — and you can see the actual Space Shuttle Endeavour. Incredible for families.
must_try: Space Shuttle Endeavour exhibit.

name: DATALAND — Museum of AI Arts
address: The Grand LA, 100 S Grand Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90012
description: Refik Anadol's world-first Museum of AI Arts. Five galleries, 25,000 sq ft of immersive digital art at Frank Gehry's Grand LA.
must_try: The immersive main gallery.

name: Grammy Museum
address: 800 W Olympic Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90015
description: Interactive music museum at LA Live. Record your own song, see iconic instruments and costumes.
must_try: The interactive sound rooms.

name: LACMA
description: Largest art museum in the West. The new David Geffen Galleries opened April 2026 — a generational expansion.
must_try: Chris Burden's Urban Light installation at dusk (free, outdoor).

name: Lucas Museum of Narrative Art
description: George Lucas's billion-dollar museum of visual storytelling opening 2026. Film, illustration, comics, digital art. Free admission.
must_try: Opening exhibitions.

name: Natural History Museum of LA
address: 900 W Exposition Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90007
description: Dinosaurs, gems, nature gardens. Free first Tuesday of each month.
must_try: Dinosaur Hall and the Nature Gardens.

name: Petersen Automotive Museum
description: Car culture is LA culture. Stunning building, incredible collection from classic to hypercar.
must_try: The Vault tour (extra $) for the real gems.

name: The Broad
address: 221 S Grand Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90012
description: Contemporary art museum — Koons, Basquiat, Warhol, and the Infinity Mirror Room. Free general admission.
must_try: Yayoi Kusama's Infinity Mirror Room (timed tickets).

name: The Getty Center
address: 1200 Getty Center Dr, Los Angeles, CA 90049
description: An architectural marvel perched above the 405. Stunning gardens, city views, and a world-class collection. Admission free.
must_try: The Central Garden and Van Gogh's Irises.

name: The Getty Villa
address: 17985 Pacific Coast Hwy, Pacific Palisades, CA 90272
description: Roman villa recreation with Greek, Roman, and Etruscan antiquities. Gardens and architecture are stunning.
must_try: Outer peristyle garden overlooking the Pacific.

name: Warner Bros Studio Tour
description: Walk the actual backlot, see the Friends set, and explore the DC Universe exhibit. More intimate than Universal.
must_try: The backlot walking tour.

name: Highland Park Bowl
address: 5621 N Figueroa St, Los Angeles, CA 90042
description: Restored 1927 bowling alley turned cocktail bar. Live music, Italian food, and gorgeous Art Deco lanes.
must_try: Bowl a game and grab a Negroni.

name: Angel City Brewery
address: 216 S Alameda St, Los Angeles, CA 90012
description: Arts District brewery in a converted warehouse. Big outdoor patio, rotating food trucks, weekend events.
must_try: Angel City IPA on the patio.

name: The Abbey
address: 692 N Robertson Blvd, West Hollywood, CA 90069
description: WeHo's most famous LGBTQ+ venue. Multiple bars, dance floors, food, and brunch. An institution.
must_try: Sunday brunch drag show.

name: Death & Co
address: 300 S Santa Fe Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90013
description: NYC cocktail institution's LA outpost in the Arts District. Dark, moody, and impeccably made drinks.
must_try: Oaxaca Old Fashioned.

name: Good Times at Davey Wayne's
address: 1611 N El Centro Ave, Hollywood, CA 90028
description: Enter through a fridge into a 70s garage-sale themed bar. Frozen drinks, yard games, and pure nostalgic chaos.
must_try: Frozen Irish Coffee.

name: No Vacancy
description: Speakeasy in a restored Victorian — enter through a bedroom, down a staircase. Live music, burlesque, strong cocktails.
must_try: Absinthe cocktail and whatever show is on.

name: The Dresden
address: 1760 N Vermont Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90027
description: Mid-century lounge made famous by Swingers. Marty & Elayne have been performing jazz/lounge here since 1982.
must_try: Blood & Sand cocktail while Marty & Elayne play.

name: The Roger Room
address: 370 N La Cienega Blvd, West Hollywood, CA 90048
description: Hidden speakeasy on La Cienega. Dark, intimate, excellent cocktails. No sign — look for the door.
must_try: Dealer's choice — tell the bartender what you like.

name: Groundlings Theatre
description: LA's legendary improv school and theater. Where Melissa McCarthy, Will Ferrell, and Kristen Wiig started.
must_try: Sunday Company show.

name: The Comedy Store
description: Legendary Sunset Strip comedy club. Three rooms, shows nightly. Pryor, Chappelle, and whoever drops in tonight.
must_try: The Original Room lineup — you never know who'll show up.

name: The Laugh Factory
description: Sunset Strip comedy institution. Nightly lineups mix headliners and up-and-comers with regular celebrity drop-ins.
must_try: Late show on a Friday.

name: HMS Bounty
description: Dark, nautical-themed dive attached to the Gaylord hotel on Wilshire. Cheap stiff drinks and a cast of regulars since 1962.
must_try: Whatever's cheapest — it's a dive.

name: Jumbo's Clown Room
description: Burlesque dive bar where dancers perform to rock and hip-hop. Cash only, no photos, unforgettable.
must_try: Cheap drinks, tip the dancers.

name: Tiki-Ti
description: Family-run since 1961 — 12 seats, 90 tropical drinks, and zero pretension. The smallest, most beloved bar in LA.
must_try: Ray's Mistake.

name: Pharaoh Karaoke Lounge
description: Koreatown noraebang institution. Private rooms, BYOB, massive Korean and English song libraries.
must_try: Book a room, bring soju from the liquor store.

name: Blue Note LA
description: The storied NYC jazz club opened on Sunset in 2025. World-class jazz, R&B, and soul in an intimate room.
must_try: Any headline act — the room is incredible.

name: The Greek Theatre
address: 2700 N Vermont Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90027
description: 5,900-seat amphitheater in Griffith Park. More intimate than the Bowl, every seat feels close.
must_try: Hike Griffith Park before the show.

name: The Hollywood Bowl
description: Most iconic outdoor music venue in America. Bring wine and a picnic. Summer season June-September.
must_try: Any show — the experience transcends the performer.

name: The Troubadour
address: 9081 Santa Monica Blvd, West Hollywood, CA 90069
description: Where Elton John played his US debut. Intimate 500-capacity room that still books the best indie and rock.
must_try: Any show — the sound is perfect for the room.

name: The Viper Room
address: 8852 W Sunset Blvd, West Hollywood, CA 90069
description: Legendary Sunset Strip rock club. Small, sweaty, loud — the way live music should be.
must_try: Catch whoever's playing.

name: Whisky A Go Go
description: The Doors' residency venue. Where LA rock was born. Still books live acts nightly.
must_try: Any live show — the history is in the walls.

name: Perch
address: 448 S Hill St, Los Angeles, CA 90013
description: DTLA rooftop with stunning city views, French bistro food, and live jazz. The skyline at night is the real menu.
must_try: Any cocktail with the view.

name: Spire 73
address: 633 W 5th St, 73rd Floor, Los Angeles, CA 90071
description: Highest open-air bar in the Western Hemisphere. 73 floors up with 360° views of the LA basin.
must_try: Any cocktail — the view is the real menu.

name: Bub & Grandma's
description: Andy Kadin's sourdough bakery empire. Expanded to pizza in the former Town Pizza space. Excellent everything.
must_try: Sourdough croissant and the pizza.

name: Clark Street Bread
address: 3101 Silver Lake Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90039
description: Artisan bread and pastries in a tiny Silver Lake space. The country loaf is legendary among Eastside bread nerds.
must_try: Country loaf and morning bun.

name: Proof Bakery
description: Atwater Village neighborhood bakery with the best croissants on the Eastside. Everything is baked fresh daily.
must_try: Almond croissant and seasonal fruit galette.

name: Dayglow Coffee
description: Light, bright Melrose coffee shop with some of the best filter coffee in the city. Minimalist design, maximum quality.
must_try: Filter coffee flight.

name: Go Get Em Tiger
address: 230 N Larchmont Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90004
description: Larchmont's buzzy coffee bar. Excellent espresso and a signature macadamia milk latte.
must_try: Macadamia milk latte.

name: Intelligentsia Coffee
address: 3922 W Sunset Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90029
description: The Silver Lake flagship that helped launch third-wave coffee in LA. Still excellent.
must_try: Black Cat espresso blend.

name: Verve Coffee Roasters
address: 833 S Spring St, Los Angeles, CA 90014
description: Santa Cruz transplant with a gorgeous DTLA space. Bright, fruit-forward roasts and serious pour-overs.
must_try: Single-origin pour-over.

name: Mashti Malone's
address: 1525 N La Brea Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90028
description: Persian ice cream since 1980. Rosewater, saffron, orange blossom — flavors you won't find anywhere else.
must_try: Rosewater and saffron pistachio.

name: Salt & Straw
address: 240 N Larchmont Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90004
description: Portland ice cream institution with wild monthly rotating flavors. Lines are real but they let you sample everything.
must_try: Sea salt with caramel ribbons, plus whatever the monthly special is.

name: Wanderlust Creamery
description: Globally-inspired ice cream — ube malted crunch, sticky rice mango, Japanese milk bread. Wildly creative.
must_try: Ube malted crunch.

name: HomeState
address: 5510 N Figueroa St, Los Angeles, CA 90042
description: Texas-style breakfast tacos and queso that Highland Park is obsessed with. Simple, perfect.
must_try: The Houston and queso.

name: Republique
address: 624 S La Brea Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90036
description: All-day French-Californian in a gorgeous Charlie Chaplin-era building. The pastry case alone is worth the trip.
must_try: Weekend brunch — short rib hash and any pastry.

name: Sqirl
address: 720 N Virgil Ave #4, Los Angeles, CA 90029
description: Jessica Koslow's legendary jam shop and brunch spot now does dinner. The ricotta toast changed LA breakfast culture.
must_try: Sorrel pesto rice bowl (daytime), smoked beet agnolotti (dinner).

name: Bay Cities Italian Deli
description: The Godmother sandwich has been voted best sandwich in LA for decades. Italian deli perfection since 1925.
must_try: The Godmother — Italian meats, peppers, the works.

name: Canter's Deli
address: 419 N Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90036
description: Open since 1931, 24/7. The quintessential LA Jewish deli — matzo ball soup at 2am after a show on Fairfax.
must_try: Matzo ball soup and pastrami on rye.

name: Cassia
description: Southeast Asian brasserie in Santa Monica. The kaya toast and Vietnamese-style pot-au-feu are standouts.
must_try: Kaya toast with a slow-cooked egg.

name: Gjelina
description: The Venice restaurant that defined Abbot Kinney. Seasonal, veggie-forward Californian with a legendary pizza program.
must_try: Any seasonal pizza and roasted vegetables.

name: Gjusta
description: Venice bakery-deli from the Gjelina team. Industrial-chic, always a line, always worth it. Pastries, sandwiches, smoked fish.
must_try: Almond croissant and smoked salmon plate.

name: Hermon's
description: Stunning neighborhood chophouse with Art Deco vibes between Highland Park and South Pasadena. From the Found Oyster team.
must_try: Mushroom Bourguignon and the pull-apart garlic bread.

name: Howlin' Ray's
description: Nashville hot chicken that made people wait 2+ hours in Chinatown. The spice levels are real.
must_try: Howlin' heat level sandwich — only if you mean it.

name: Howlin' Ray's (Pasadena)
description: Second location — same Nashville hot chicken, shorter line than Chinatown.
must_try: Medium heat sandwich.

name: Langer's Delicatessen
address: 704 S Alvarado St, Los Angeles, CA 90057
description: Since 1947. Many argue the #19 pastrami sandwich is better than Katz's. Hot pastrami, Swiss, coleslaw, Russian dressing on double-baked rye.
must_try: #19 pastrami sandwich.

name: Max & Helen's
address: 127 N Larchmont Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90004
description: Phil Rosenthal and Nancy Silverton's old-school diner bringing elevated comfort food to Larchmont. Opened late 2025.
must_try: The Larchmont Slam breakfast.

name: Porto's Bakery & Cafe
description: Cuban bakery institution with lines out the door daily. The cheese rolls and potato balls are cheap thrills Angelenos are addicted to.
must_try: Cheese roll (refugiado) and guava strudel.

name: Wilde's
description: 2026's toughest reservation. British comfort food meets Californian soul in Los Feliz. Daytime bakery with scones.
must_try: The rotating daily meat pie.

name: Wurstküche
description: Exotic sausages (rattlesnake-rabbit, pheasant) with Belgian fries and craft beer in the Arts District.
must_try: Rattlesnake-rabbit sausage with mango-habanero sauce.

name: Zankou Chicken
description: Armenian rotisserie chicken chain that's an LA essential. The garlic sauce is legendary and addictive.
must_try: Half chicken with garlic sauce.

name: Din Tai Fung
description: The OG US location of the Taiwanese soup dumpling empire. Still the benchmark for xiao long bao.
must_try: Pork xiao long bao (soup dumplings).

name: Lunasia Dim Sum House
description: Massive, overflowing dim sum served all day. Some of the largest and most generous har gow and siu mai in the SGV.
must_try: Jumbo pork siu mai and macadamia nut egg tarts.

name: Newport Seafood
address: 518 W Las Tunas Dr, San Gabriel, CA 91776
description: Famous for the Special House Lobster — wok-fried with butter, garlic, and green onion. A SGV institution.
must_try: Special House Lobster.

name: Pine & Crane
address: 1521 Griffith Park Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90026
description: Elevated Taiwanese in Silver Lake. The dan dan noodles and three-cup chicken are neighborhood staples.
must_try: Dan dan noodles and mapo tofu.

name: Sea Harbour Seafood Restaurant
description: Heavyweight SGV dim sum. Forget the carts — everything is ordered off a menu and steamed fresh to order.
must_try: Har gow (shrimp dumplings) and baked BBQ pork buns.

name: Meals by Genet
address: 1053 S Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90019
description: The crown jewel of Little Ethiopia. Chef Genet's vegetarian combination is one of the great meals in LA.
must_try: Vegetarian combination platter.

name: Bavel
description: Middle Eastern fine dining from the Bestia team. The lamb neck shawarma is one of the best dishes in the city, full stop.
must_try: Lamb neck shawarma with pomegranate and tahini.

name: Kato
address: 777 S Alameda St, Los Angeles, CA 90021
description: Taiwanese-American tasting menu at ROW DTLA. Chef Jon Yao elevates SGV flavors to Michelin-level artistry. James Beard Best Chef California.
must_try: Tapioca boba with brown butter and caviar.

name: Lielle
address: 9575 W Pico Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90035
description: Swedish chef Marcus Jernmark's 2026 fine-dining debut. Four-course bistronomy menu changing every five weeks. Relaxed Scandinavian elegance.
must_try: Aged striped jack with gooseberry.

name: Musso & Frank Grill
description: Hollywood's oldest restaurant (1919). Red leather booths, martinis stirred by bartenders who've been here 40 years.
must_try: Flannel cakes at lunch, martini anytime.

name: Providence
description: Three-Michelin-star seafood tasting menu. Chef Michael Cimarusti's temple to sustainable seafood — one of only two three-stars in LA.
must_try: Chef's tasting menu — let them drive.

name: Sushi Ginza Onodera
address: 609 N La Cienega Blvd, West Hollywood, CA 90069
description: Omakase at the highest level — fish flown from Tsukiji, rice seasoned with red vinegar. Where sushi chefs eat on their night off.
must_try: 20+ course omakase — seasonal.

name: Grand Central Market
description: Open since 1917. A DTLA food hall before food halls were a thing. 30+ vendors from tacos to Thai to egg sandwiches.
must_try: Egg sandwich from Eggslut, tacos from Tacos Tumbras a Tomas.

name: Petit Trois
address: 718 N Highland Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90038
description: Ludo Lefebvre's no-reservations French bistro with a tiny counter. The omelette is deceptively simple and unforgettable.
must_try: Bourguignon double cheeseburger and French omelette.

name: Animal
address: 435 N Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90036
description: Jon & Vinny's meat-forward original. Pork belly, foie gras, pig ear — this is where the Fairfax food strip started.
must_try: Pork belly sliders and bacon chocolate crunch bar.

name: Badmaash
description: Modern Indian from the Mehendro brothers — third location opened in Venice 2026. Buttered chicken is cult-followed.
must_try: Butter chicken and chicken tikka poutine.

name: Bad Roman
address: 267 N Canon Dr, Suite A7, Beverly Hills, CA 90210
description: NYC's maximalist, playful Italian taking over the historic Palm Restaurant space. Loud decor, strong drinks, pure fun.
must_try: The Bad Ombré cocktail and tiramisu ice cream cake.

name: BAR di Bello
address: 3300 W Sunset Blvd, Ste 110, Los Angeles, CA 90026
description: Milanese-inspired bar and restaurant bringing aperitivo culture and massive Negronis to Sunset Row in Silver Lake.
must_try: Negroni di Basso and Penne di Bello.

name: Bestia
description: Industrial-chic Arts District Italian that's been the hardest reservation in LA for a decade. House-made pasta and wood-fired pizza are legit.
must_try: Spaghetti Rustichella with Dungeness crab.

name: Cosa Buona
address: 2100 W Sunset Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90026
description: Echo Park red-sauce Italian done right. NYC-style slices and perfect meatball subs.
must_try: Meatball parm sub.

name: Felix
description: Evan Funke's handmade pasta temple on Abbot Kinney. Watch the pasta being rolled through the glass window.
must_try: Cacio e pepe and any fresh pasta.

name: Jon & Vinny's
address: 412 N Fairfax Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90036
description: The casual sibling of Animal — Italian-American comfort food on Fairfax. All-day menu, always packed.
must_try: Vodka pizza and garlic knots.

name: Daikokuya
description: The ramen line that never dies. Rich tonkotsu broth in a tiny Little Tokyo shop. No substitutes.
must_try: Original Daikokuya ramen with extra chashu.

name: Marugame Monzo
description: Handmade udon pulled fresh behind a glass window. The uni cream udon is outrageously good.
must_try: Uni cream udon.

name: Silverlake Ramen
description: The Eastside ramen spot. Rich tonkotsu in a hip Silver Lake space. Always a line, always worth it.
must_try: Original Silverlake Ramen with extra egg.

name: Sushi Gen
description: Little Tokyo legend. The sashimi lunch special ($20 for a huge plate) has had a line since the 90s.
must_try: Sashimi deluxe lunch special.

name: Sushisamba
address: 639 N La Peer Dr, West Hollywood, CA 90069
description: Massive 2026 opening in WeHo blending Japanese, Brazilian, and Peruvian cuisine on a sprawling rooftop with retractable roof.
must_try: Robata grill selections and signature ceviche.

name: Kang Ho-dong Baekjeong
description: Celebrity-chef KBBQ chain with a fun, energetic vibe. Known for thick-cut pork belly and corn cheese.
must_try: Thick-cut pork belly and egg soufflé.

name: Park's BBQ
address: 955 S Vermont Ave G, Los Angeles, CA 90006
description: The gold standard for traditional KBBQ in Los Angeles. Unmatched meat quality and the best banchan spread in town.
must_try: Galbi (marinated short rib).

name: Quarters Korean BBQ
description: Loud, trendy, and incredibly popular. Tapas-style KBBQ approach in the bustling Chapman Plaza. Walk-in friendly.
must_try: Korean cheese fondue to dip your meat.

name: Broken Spanish Comedor
description: Chef Ray Garcia's triumphant 2026 return. Reimagining Alta California cuisine with modern Mexican soul. Best new opening in LA.
must_try: Albondigas with duck and bacon, crispy chicharrón in garlic mojo.

name: Guelaguetza
address: 3014 W Olympic Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90006
description: The absolute pinnacle of Oaxacan food in America. James Beard America's Classic award. Massive, lively space with live music.
must_try: Festival de Moles and a michelada.

name: Guerrilla Tacos
description: Chef Wes Avila turned a taco cart into an Arts District institution. Elevated street food with seasonal ingredients.
must_try: Sweet potato taco with feta and almond chile.

name: Guisados
address: 2100 E Cesar Chavez Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90033
description: Famous for thick, handmade tortillas loaded with slow-braised stews. The original Boyle Heights location is essential.
must_try: Taco sampler plate (6 mini tacos).

name: Raffi's Place
description: Glendale's Persian kebab institution. Massive portions of koobideh and joojeh over saffron rice.
must_try: Sultani combo (koobideh + barg).

name: Connie & Ted's
address: 8171 Santa Monica Blvd, West Hollywood, CA 90046
description: New England-style raw bar and seafood house in WeHo. Whole lobsters, steamers, and a raw bar that rivals the East Coast.
must_try: Lobster roll (hot butter) and raw bar platter.

name: Marea Beverly Hills
address: 255 N Camden Dr, Beverly Hills, CA 90210
description: NYC import — Italian seafood at the highest level. The fusilli with bone marrow and octopus is a signature.
must_try: Fusilli with red wine braised octopus and bone marrow.

name: Nobu Malibu
description: The OG oceanfront Nobu. Expensive, celebrity-heavy, but the black cod miso with the Pacific 30 feet away is genuinely special.
must_try: Black cod miso.

name: Mariscos Jalisco
address: 3040 E Olympic Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90023
description: Ground zero for crispy shrimp tacos dorados. Raul Ortega's truck put Boyle Heights on the food map.
must_try: Shrimp tacos dorados — accept no substitutes.

name: Jitlada
description: Legendary Southern Thai in a Hollywood strip mall. Punishing, unapologetic heat and incredibly complex curries.
must_try: Jazz Burger, Green Curry, and Morning Glory Salad.

name: Night + Market Song
address: 3322 W Sunset Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90026
description: Kris Yenbamroong's loud, funky Thai street food joint. The larb and pad see ew are essential.
must_try: Startled Pig (fried pork jowl).

name: Sapp Coffee Shop
description: Thai Town strip mall legend. The jade noodle and boat noodle soups are some of the best $10 meals in the city.
must_try: Jade noodle soup.

name: Crossroads Kitchen
description: Celebrity-chef Tal Ronnen's upscale vegan Mediterranean. Even non-vegans are impressed.
must_try: Artichoke oysters and truffle pasta.

name: BMO Stadium
address: 3939 S Figueroa St, Los Angeles, CA 90037
description: Home of LAFC. The most electric soccer atmosphere in the US — The 3252 supporters section is legendary.
must_try: Stand in the supporters section if you can handle the energy.

name: Crypto.com Arena
address: 1111 S Figueroa St, Los Angeles, CA 90015
description: Home of the Lakers, Kings, and Sparks. Also hosts major concerts year-round. Part of the LA Live complex.
must_try: Lakers game if they're in town.

name: Dodger Stadium
address: 1000 Vin Scully Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90012
description: Third-oldest MLB stadium, gorgeous Elysian Park setting. Dodger Dogs and the best sunset in baseball.
must_try: Dodger Dog and a beer in the outfield pavilion with the sunset.
hours: Game days, gates 2hrs before first pitch

name: Intuit Dome
description: Brand-new Clippers arena. Opened 2024 — most technologically advanced arena in the world. Hosted 2026 NBA All-Star.
must_try: The Halo Board — 360° wraparound LED screen.

name: SoFi Stadium
description: The most expensive stadium ever built. Hub for 2026 FIFA World Cup matches including US opener June 12.
must_try: A stadium tour if you can't catch a game.

name: Hollywood Pantages Theatre
description: Art Deco theater hosting Broadway touring productions. Hamilton, Wicked, and whatever's next.
must_try: Whatever Broadway touring show is running.

name: Downtown LA Proper
description: Spectacularly designed by Kelly Wearstler. Two restaurants from Suzanne Goin and Caroline Styne, including a stunning rooftop.
must_try: Sunset drinks at Cara Cara rooftop.

name: Freehand Los Angeles
description: DTLA boutique with private rooms and shared dorms. The rooftop bar (Broken Shaker) is one of the best in the city.
must_try: Drinks at Broken Shaker rooftop.

name: Hotel Figueroa
address: 939 S Figueroa St, Los Angeles, CA 90015
description: Historic 1926 hotel with a Moroccan-meets-California aesthetic. Pool courtyard is stunning.
must_try: Poolside cocktails at the Veranda.

name: Mama Shelter Los Angeles
description: Fun, colorful boutique in Hollywood. Great rooftop bar and restaurant. Best value design hotel.
must_try: Rooftop bar.

name: Santa Monica Proper
description: Design-forward boutique steps from the beach. Rooftop pool, excellent restaurant (Calabra).
must_try: Rooftop pool and Calabra for dinner.

name: Chateau Marmont
description: The most storied hotel in Hollywood. Members-only now, but if you can get in, you're living in the myth.
must_try: Dinner in the garden.

name: Hollywood Roosevelt
description: Site of the first Academy Awards (1929). The pool and Tropicana bar are classic Hollywood scene.
must_try: Tropicana Pool & Café.

name: Sunset Tower Hotel
description: True Hollywood classic. Historic Art Deco building with understated glamour and an elite bar scene favored by industry.
must_try: The Tower Bar for celebrity spotting.

name: The Beverly Hilton
description: Home of the Golden Globes. Classic Beverly Hills luxury with the iconic pool.
must_try: Pool day with cabana.

name: Waldorf Astoria Beverly Hills
description: The newest ultra-luxury in Beverly Hills. Rooftop pool, Baldi steakhouse (new 2026), and views of the Hollywood Hills.
must_try: Baldi Tuscan steakhouse (Edo Baldi's 2026 opening).

name: Shutters on the Beach
description: THE beachfront hotel in LA. Directly on Santa Monica Beach, white-washed luxury.
must_try: Beach-facing room at sunrise.

name: The Langham Huntington
address: 1401 S Oak Knoll Ave, Pasadena, CA 91106
description: Grand Pasadena resort with Japanese garden, spa, and gorgeous grounds. A world away from LA's chaos.
must_try: Afternoon tea and the Japanese Garden.

name: El Matador State Beach
description: Dramatic sea caves and rock formations. The most photogenic beach in LA — small, secluded, feels like another planet.
must_try: Sunset through the sea caves.

name: Manhattan Beach
description: Where locals go. Volleyball culture, the Strand bike path, and a charming downtown walkable from the sand.
must_try: Walk the pier at sunset, then dinner on Manhattan Beach Blvd.

name: Santa Monica Beach & Pier
address: 200 Santa Monica Pier, Santa Monica, CA 90401
description: End of Route 66. Ferris wheel, roller coaster, arcade, street performers. Touristy but iconic — sunset from the pier is worth it.
must_try: Ride the Pacific Wheel at sunset.

name: Venice Beach Boardwalk
description: The freak show boardwalk — street performers, Muscle Beach, skate park, drum circles at sunset.
must_try: Sunday sunset drum circle.

name: The Strand (Marvin Braude Bike Trail)
description: 22-mile paved coastal bike path. The quintessential LA ride — ocean on one side, beach culture on the other.
must_try: Rent a cruiser in Santa Monica and ride to Manhattan Beach.

name: Eaton Canyon Falls
description: Easy 3.5-mile roundtrip hike to a 40-foot waterfall. Best after winter rains.
must_try: Visit after rain for the best water flow.

name: Runyon Canyon Park
address: 2000 N Fuller Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90046
description: THE LA hike. 3-mile loop with panoramic city views. Dog-friendly, social, bring water. Best at sunrise.
must_try: Full loop to the top for the 360° view.

name: Temescal Gateway Park
description: 3.8-mile loop to a ridge with ocean views. Moderate difficulty, shaded sections.
must_try: Full Temescal Ridge loop for canyon-to-ocean views.

name: Topanga State Park
description: The largest state park within the boundaries of a city. Trails range from easy fire roads to rugged canyon hikes with ocean views.
must_try: Los Liones Trail to Parker Mesa Overlook.

name: Griffith Park
address: 4730 Crystal Springs Dr, Los Angeles, CA 90027
description: 4,310 acres — one of the largest urban parks in North America. Trails to Hollywood Sign, Observatory, Zoo, and Autry Museum.
must_try: Hike to the Hollywood Sign via Mt. Hollywood Trail.

name: Surfrider Beach
description: World Surfing Reserve. First Point is where LA's surf culture was born. Watch from the pier or rent a board.
must_try: Golden hour from the Malibu Pier.

name: Erewhon Market
description: LA's infamously expensive, immaculately curated health food store. Part grocery, part celebrity hangout, part tourist attraction.
must_try: A celebrity collab smoothie and the hot bar.

name: Trader Joe's
description: LA-born grocery chain. Cheap wine, great snacks, best value grocery run for stocking a rental.
must_try: Everything Bagel Seasoning and whatever seasonal item is trending.

name: Healthy Spot
description: LA's dog care chain — daycare, grooming, and boutique. LA is extremely dog-friendly and this is the go-to.
must_try: Day camp while you explore.

name: Abbot Kinney Boulevard
description: Dubbed the 'coolest block in America.' A mile of high-end boutiques, surf lifestyle shops, and top-tier restaurants.
must_try: First Friday food truck events.

name: Rodeo Drive
description: Luxury shopping strip — Chanel, Vuitton, Gucci. Even if you're not buying, the people-watching and architecture are worth a stroll.
must_try: Window shopping and a photo at the iconic sign.

name: The Grove + Original Farmers Market
address: 189 The Grove Dr / 6333 W 3rd St, Los Angeles, CA 90036
description: Open-air shopping center next to the historic 1934 Farmers Market. Combine mainstream brands with Bob's Donuts and Du-par's.
must_try: Original Farmers Market next door — 100+ vendors since 1934.

name: Melrose Trading Post
description: Essential Sunday ritual. Open-air flea market with vintage clothing, antique furniture, local artisans, and live music.
must_try: Vintage denim hunting.

name: Rose Bowl Flea Market
description: 2nd Sunday of every month — 2,500+ vendors. The best flea market on the West Coast.
must_try: Get there at 5am for VIP early access ($25).

name: Santee Alley
address: 210 E Olympic Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90015
description: The heart of LA's Fashion District. Chaotic open-air market selling everything cheap — clothing, accessories, electronics. Bring cash.
must_try: Haggle for deals on everything.

name: Melrose Avenue (Fairfax to La Brea)
description: Streetwear, vintage, and Instagram murals. Supreme, Round Two, and dozens of independent shops.
must_try: Paul Smith's pink wall photo and vintage shopping at Round Two.

name: Wi Spa
description: The most famous 24/7 co-ed Korean spa in LA. Multiple mineral saunas, open jjimjilbang, and a great café.
must_try: The full body scrub (demata).

name: The NOW Massage
address: Multiple locations (Silver Lake, WeHo, Venice, Studio City)
description: Drop-in massage boutique with Instagram-worthy interiors. 25/50/75-minute sessions, no membership.
must_try: 50-min custom massage.
